newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela attorney general quits over lack of help.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela attorney general quits over lack of help.

text.p: Venezuela's Attorney General resigned on Friday, saying he was tired of the lack of cooperation he received from government ministers.

Jesus Petit Da Costa told a news conference that some members of President Rafael Caldera's cabinet had hindered his work, including efforts to extradite scores of bankers who fled justice during the collapse of the financial sector in 1994.
"I cannot hide my displeasure that there has not been a single extradition," he said.

Da Costa, attorney general since the start of Caldera's term in February 1994, blamed a "society of accomplices" in the government, whom he did not name, for lack of progress in improving Venezuela's justice record.
"The society of accomplices is responsible for the impunity of crimes and this impunity suffocates the people's faith in democracy," he said.
Da Costa said he would remain at his post until Caldera named a successor.
